profile.description: EXAMPLE PROFILE for the cross-project neutrality test. businessContext.summary: Multi-brand promotional storefront where discovery and deal clarity drive conversion; the homepage is a dense, scannable offer surface, not a story.
businessContext.audience: Deal-driven shoppers browsing across brands and categories
businessContext.commerceStrategy: commerce-first: compact hero, campaign and category discovery, high product density, explicit offer communication where business data is real

sources.note: Placeholder for a future client file. Deliberately EXCLUDES the Home page draft (121:14313): its brand-first hero contradicts this aesthetic, proving scope selection is a profile decision, not core behavior.

aesthetic.direction: Commerce promotional: sans-serif-led hierarchy, compact hero, card-based product grids at high density, strong offer typographic contrast, category tiles over editorial spreads. Same component vocabulary as the luxury profile — density and emphasis change, not the system.

referenceDesigns.label: Promo Homepage exploration (PL drafts, archived)
referenceDesigns.note: Historic draft direction only — reference, not an approved source; PL file is issue #2's archive concern.

constraints: No serif display roles; sans throughout with weight/size contrast.
Offers, badges, and countdowns appear ONLY where the client's business data actually supports them (fixture policy below) — never as decorative fiction.
Higher component reuse ratio than luxury profile: grids repeat card instances.

pages.name: 01 — Foundation
pages.purpose: Tokens reference composed from normalized contracts under the promotional direction.

pages.name: 02 — Homepage (responsive)
pages.purpose: One responsive page at 1440/768/390: slim header, compact campaign hero, category grid, promo product grid, multi-brand strip — instances and variants only.

content.fixturePolicy: Product cards render with placeholder art and clearly-fake 'SAMPLE' pricing tokens only if the client profile enables them; no real-looking prices, % discounts, stock counts, review scores, or urgency timers — this storefront's value proposition is offers, so fictional offers are the worst possible fixture. Client onboarding must supply real offer data policy before any commerce content composes.
